modules.name: stat/ising/ising_mc
modules.src:
###
The two-dimensional Ising model on an L by L square lattice with periodic
edges, sampled by Metropolis (checkerboard order) or Wolff clusters at
temperature T, coupling J and field h. A run returns the energy per site,
|m|, the susceptibility, the specific heat and Binder's cumulant with error
bars from binning, the autocorrelation times, the time series and the final
spins, beside the exact results it can be checked against: Onsager's T_c and
infinite-lattice energy, Yang's spontaneous magnetization, and Kaufman's
energy and specific heat of the same finite lattice. Every random number is
a Philox4x32-10 word of a counter, so a run is bit-identical in every engine.
###
# The program behind `viv export stat/ising/ising_mc.export.toml`: the
# settings at the top level, one call of lib/ising's simulate, and its
# measurements copied into the globals below. A parameter left out of a run
# keeps the value here.
#
#     viv run stat/ising/ising_mc.viv
#
# The energy of an arrangement is E = -J sum_<ij> s_i s_j - h sum_i s_i and
# its weight exp(-E / T), with Boltzmann's constant 1.
from ising import critical_temperature, simulate, kaufman_energy_heat, onsager_energy, yang_magnetization

#: size  L, the lattice's side: N = L * L spins, periodic edges; even, so the checkerboard's two colors alternate around the wrap
size: Int = 16
#: temperature  T, in units of J / k_B when J = 1; beta = 1 / T
temperature = 2.0
#: coupling  J, between neighbors: positive is ferromagnetic (Wolff needs J > 0)
coupling = 1.0
#: field  h, the external field
field = 0.0
#: algorithm  "metropolis": single-spin flips in checkerboard order; "wolff": cluster flips
algorithm = "metropolis"
#: start  "cold": every spin up; "hot": each spin up or down at random
start = "cold"
#: sweeps  the measured sweeps; a Wolff sweep is as many clusters as add up to N spins or more
sweeps: Int = 2000
#: thermalization  the sweeps run and discarded before measuring
thermalization: Int = 500
#: seed  the Philox key: runs with the same seed and settings give the same bits
seed: Int = 1
#: bins  the number of bins for the error bars; each holds sweeps / bins sweeps, which should be many autocorrelation times
bins: Int = 20

if size % 2 != 0 {
    stop(f"size must be even for the checkerboard; it is {size}")
}
if temperature <= 0.0 {
    stop(f"temperature must be positive; it is {temperature}")
}
if bins < 2 or bins > sweeps {
    stop(f"bins must be between 2 and sweeps ({sweeps}); it is {bins}")
}
if algorithm == "wolff" and coupling <= 0.0 {
    stop(f"Wolff clusters need a ferromagnetic coupling > 0; it is {coupling}")
}

beta = 1.0 / temperature
run = simulate(size, beta, coupling, field, algorithm == "wolff", sweeps, thermalization, seed, start == "hot", bins)

# ---- what the run measured
#: energy  the energy per site, <E> / N
energy = run.stats.energy
#: energy_err  its standard error, from the scatter of the bin means
energy_err = run.stats.energy_err
#: mag_abs  <|m|>, m = sum_i s_i / N
mag_abs = run.stats.mag_abs
#: mag_abs_err  its standard error, from the bins
mag_abs_err = run.stats.mag_abs_err
#: mag  <m>, which is near 0 at h = 0 on a finite lattice once the run flips between up and down
mag = run.stats.mag
#: mag_err  its standard error, from the bins
mag_err = run.stats.mag_err
#: heat  the specific heat per site, beta^2 N (<e^2> - <e>^2), e = E / N
heat = run.stats.heat
#: heat_err  its jackknife error over the bins
heat_err = run.stats.heat_err
#: chi  the susceptibility per site, beta N (<m^2> - <|m|>^2)
chi = run.stats.chi
#: chi_err  its jackknife error over the bins
chi_err = run.stats.chi_err
#: binder  Binder's cumulant 1 - <m^4> / (3 <m^2>^2): 2/3 when ordered, 0 for a Gaussian m
binder = run.stats.binder
#: binder_err  its jackknife error over the bins
binder_err = run.stats.binder_err
#: tau_energy  the integrated autocorrelation time of the energy, in sweeps
tau_energy = run.stats.tau_energy
#: tau_mag  the integrated autocorrelation time of |m|, in sweeps
tau_mag = run.stats.tau_mag
#: accept  Metropolis: the fraction of proposed flips accepted; Wolff: the mean cluster size over N
accept = run.accept
#: energy_series  the energy per site after each measured sweep
energy_series = run.es
#: mag_series  m after each measured sweep
mag_series = run.ms
#: spins  the final arrangement, L by L, each +1 or -1
spins = run.spins

# ---- the exact results to hold the run to
#: t_critical  Onsager's critical temperature 2 J / ln(1 + sqrt 2) (for J > 0)
t_critical = critical_temperature(abs(coupling))
#: exact_known  whether exact_energy, exact_heat and energy_infinite apply: field 0, coupling positive and temperature not T_c
exact_known = field == 0.0 and coupling > 0.0 and temperature != t_critical
#: exact_energy  Kaufman's exact energy per site of this L by L lattice (0 unless exact_known)
exact_energy = 0.0
#: exact_heat  Kaufman's exact specific heat per site of this L by L lattice (0 unless exact_known)
exact_heat = 0.0
#: energy_infinite  Onsager's energy per site of the infinite lattice (0 unless exact_known)
energy_infinite = 0.0
#: mag_infinite  Yang's spontaneous magnetization of the infinite lattice at h = 0: 0 at and above T_c
mag_infinite = yang_magnetization(beta, abs(coupling))
if exact_known {
    exact_energy, exact_heat = kaufman_energy_heat(size, beta, coupling)
    energy_infinite = onsager_energy(beta, coupling)
}

show energy, energy_err, exact_energy
show mag_abs, mag_abs_err, mag_infinite
show heat, heat_err, exact_heat
show chi, chi_err, binder, binder_err
show tau_energy, tau_mag, accept

# ---- what holds for every run, whatever the settings (the statistical
# checks against the exact results are in stat/ising/test_ising.py, which
# chooses runs long enough for them)
test "every spin is +1 or -1, and the series have one entry per measured sweep" {
    for i to size {
        for j to size {
            assert_near(abs(spins[i, j]), 1.0, 0.0)
        }
    }
    assert_near(len(energy_series), sweeps, 0.0)
    assert_near(len(mag_series), sweeps, 0.0)
}
test "the energy per site lies in [-2 |J| - |h|, 2 |J| + |h|] and |m| in [0, 1]" {
    bound = 2.0 * abs(coupling) + abs(field)
    assert_true(energy >= -bound and energy <= bound)
    assert_true(mag_abs >= 0.0 and mag_abs <= 1.0)
    assert_true(abs(mag) <= mag_abs)
}
test "the variances are not negative, Binder's cumulant is at most 2/3, and tau is at least 1/2" {
    # <m^4> >= <m^2>^2 makes U <= 2/3; tau = 1/2 + a sum that the window stops while positive
    assert_true(heat >= 0.0 and chi >= 0.0)
    assert_true(binder <= 2.0 / 3.0 + 1.0e-12)
    assert_true(energy_err >= 0.0 and mag_abs_err >= 0.0 and heat_err >= 0.0 and chi_err >= 0.0 and binder_err >= 0.0)
    assert_true(accept >= 0.0 and accept <= 1.0)
}

modules.name: lib/ising

defs.doc:
A whole run: `therm` sweeps discarded, then `sweeps` sweeps measured,
by Metropolis (wolff false) or by Wolff clusters (wolff true).

A Wolff sweep during thermalization is as many clusters as it takes for
their sizes to add up to N or more. A measured sweep is a fixed number of
clusters, N over the mean cluster size of the thermalization (rounded,
at least 1; 1 when there is no thermalization). The number must be
fixed: stopping each sweep when the sizes reach N makes the measurement
times depend on the clusters drawn, and that biases the averages (by 8
standard errors in the energy at L = 16, T = 2.0, before this rule).

`accept` is the fraction of proposed flips accepted (Metropolis) or the
mean cluster size over N (Wolff), over the measured sweeps.
defs.intent: A whole run: `therm` sweeps discarded, then `sweeps` sweeps measured, by Metropolis (wolff false) or by Wolff clusters (wolff true).  A Wolff sweep during thermalization is as many clusters as it takes for their sizes to add up to N or more. A measured sweep is a fixed number of clusters, N over the mean cluster size of the thermalization (rounded, at least 1; 1 when there is no thermalization). The number must be fixed: stopping each sweep when the sizes reach N makes the measurement times depend on the clusters drawn, and that biases the averages (by 8 standard errors in the energy at L = 16, T = 2.0, before this rule).  `accept` is the fraction of proposed flips accepted (Metropolis) or the mean cluster size over N (Wolff), over the measured sweeps.

defs.doc: Onsager's critical temperature, 2 J / ln(1 + sqrt 2).
defs.intent: Onsager's critical temperature, 2 J / ln(1 + sqrt 2).

defs.doc:
Yang's spontaneous magnetization of the infinite lattice,
(1 - sinh(2 beta J)^-4)^(1/8) below T_c and 0 at or above it.
defs.intent: Yang's spontaneous magnetization of the infinite lattice, (1 - sinh(2 beta J)^-4)^(1/8) below T_c and 0 at or above it.

defs.doc:
The exact energy per site and specific heat per site of the L by L
periodic lattice at h = 0: u = -(1/N) d lnZ / d beta and
c = (beta^2 / N) d^2 lnZ / d beta^2, by five-point differences of
kaufman_lnz with step 1e-3 beta (truncation of order 1e-12 relative).
defs.intent: The exact energy per site and specific heat per site of the L by L periodic lattice at h = 0: u = -(1/N) d lnZ / d beta and c = (beta^2 / N) d^2 lnZ / d beta^2, by five-point differences of kaufman_lnz with step 1e-3 beta (truncation of order 1e-12 relative).

defs.doc:
Onsager's energy per site of the infinite lattice at h = 0:
-J coth(2K) [1 + (2 / pi) (2 tanh(2K)^2 - 1) K(k)], K = beta J,
k = 2 sinh(2K) / cosh(2K)^2. Not defined at T_c itself (k = 1).
defs.intent: Onsager's energy per site of the infinite lattice at h = 0: -J coth(2K) [1 + (2 / pi) (2 tanh(2K)^2 - 1) K(k)], K = beta J, k = 2 sinh(2K) / cosh(2K)^2. Not defined at T_c itself (k = 1).

defs.doc:
The four neighbors of each site of an L by L periodic lattice, site
i * L + j at row i and column j: up, down, left, right.
defs.intent: The four neighbors of each site of an L by L periodic lattice, site i * L + j at row i and column j: up, down, left, right.

defs.doc:
The starting arrangement: every spin up ("cold"), or each spin up or down
with probability one half ("hot"), from the seed's own Philox stream.
defs.intent: The starting arrangement: every spin up ("cold"), or each spin up or down with probability one half ("hot"), from the seed's own Philox stream.

defs.doc:
The acceptance probability of flipping a spin, by the spin and the sum of
its four neighbors: entry 5 * (s + 1) / 2 + (nn + 4) / 2. A flip changes
the energy by 2 s (J nn + h) and is accepted with probability
min(1, exp(-beta dE)).
defs.intent: The acceptance probability of flipping a spin, by the spin and the sum of its four neighbors: entry 5 * (s + 1) / 2 + (nn + 4) / 2. A flip changes the energy by 2 s (J nn + h) and is accepted with probability min(1, exp(-beta dE)).

defs.doc:
One Wolff cluster update. The cluster grows from a random seed site,
adding each aligned neighbor with probability padd = 1 - exp(-2 beta J);
the whole cluster then flips, with probability min(1, exp(-2 beta h S))
when the field is on (S: the cluster's summed spin), which is the
Metropolis test of the field's energy change. Draw k of cluster number
`cluster` is word k mod 4 of the Philox block (k div 4, cluster mod 2^32,
cluster div 2^32, 0) under the key (seed, TAG_WOLFF). `stack` and `mark`
are work arrays of N entries, `mark` all zero on entry and on exit.
Returns the cluster's size, and whether it flipped.
defs.intent: One Wolff cluster update. The cluster grows from a random seed site, adding each aligned neighbor with probability padd = 1 - exp(-2 beta J); the whole cluster then flips, with probability min(1, exp(-2 beta h S)) when the field is on (S: the cluster's summed spin), which is the Metropolis test of the field's energy change. Draw k of cluster number `cluster` is word k mod 4 of the Philox block (k div 4, cluster mod 2^32, cluster div 2^32, 0) under the key (seed, TAG_WOLFF). `stack` and `mark` are work arrays of N entries, `mark` all zero on entry and on exit. Returns the cluster's size, and whether it flipped.

defs.doc:
One Metropolis sweep in checkerboard order: the sites with i + j even,
then the odd ones. Sites of one color do not touch, so the order inside a
color does not matter. Site (i, j) of color c is the q-th of its row
(j = 2 q + (i + c) mod 2) and draws word q mod 4 of the Philox block
(q div 4, i, 2 sweep + c, 0) under the key (seed, TAG_METROPOLIS).
Returns the number of flips accepted.
defs.intent: One Metropolis sweep in checkerboard order: the sites with i + j even, then the odd ones. Sites of one color do not touch, so the order inside a color does not matter. Site (i, j) of color c is the q-th of its row (j = 2 q + (i + c) mod 2) and draws word q mod 4 of the Philox block (q div 4, i, 2 sweep + c, 0) under the key (seed, TAG_METROPOLIS). Returns the number of flips accepted.

defs.doc: The energy per site and the magnetization per site of the arrangement s.
defs.intent: The energy per site and the magnetization per site of the arrangement s.

defs.doc:
The measurements of the series es (energy per site) and ms
(magnetization per site), one entry per sweep, with error bars from
`bins` equal bins (the last n mod bins sweeps are left out of the
errors only): the standard error of the bin means for the averages, and
the jackknife over bins for the specific heat, the susceptibility and
Binder's cumulant, whose central values use every sweep.
defs.intent: The measurements of the series es (energy per site) and ms (magnetization per site), one entry per sweep, with error bars from `bins` equal bins (the last n mod bins sweeps are left out of the errors only): the standard error of the bin means for the averages, and the jackknife over bins for the specific heat, the susceptibility and Binder's cumulant, whose central values use every sweep.

loops.head: for t from b * blen to (b + 1) * blen

defs.doc:
log Z of the L by L periodic lattice at h = 0, from Kaufman's exact
partition function as Ferdinand and Fisher write it:
Z = (1/2) (2 sinh 2K)^(N/2) (Z1 + Z2 + Z3 + Z4), Z1 = prod_r
2 cosh(L g_{2r+1} / 2), Z2 the same with sinh, Z3 and Z4 the same over
g_{2r}, r = 0 .. L-1; cosh g_l = cosh 2K coth 2K - cos(l pi / L) with
g_l > 0, except g_0 = 2K + ln tanh K, which changes sign at T_c.
Each product is summed as a log and a sign.
defs.intent: log Z of the L by L periodic lattice at h = 0, from Kaufman's exact partition function as Ferdinand and Fisher write it: Z = (1/2) (2 sinh 2K)^(N/2) (Z1 + Z2 + Z3 + Z4), Z1 = prod_r 2 cosh(L g_{2r+1} / 2), Z2 the same with sinh, Z3 and Z4 the same over g_{2r}, r = 0 .. L-1; cosh g_l = cosh 2K coth 2K - cos(l pi / L) with g_l > 0, except g_0 = 2K + ln tanh K, which changes sign at T_c. Each product is summed as a log and a sign.

defs.doc:
The complete elliptic integral of the first kind K(k), by the
arithmetic-geometric mean: pi / (2 agm(1, sqrt(1 - k^2))).
defs.intent: The complete elliptic integral of the first kind K(k), by the arithmetic-geometric mean: pi / (2 agm(1, sqrt(1 - k^2))).

defs.doc:
Philox4x32-10: the four 32-bit words the counter (c0, c1, c2, c3) maps to
under the key (k0, k1), as Random123's philox4x32 computes them (the
same code as examples/options/mc.viv).
defs.intent: Philox4x32-10: the four 32-bit words the counter (c0, c1, c2, c3) maps to under the key (k0, k1), as Random123's philox4x32 computes them (the same code as examples/options/mc.viv).

defs.doc:
A uniform number in (0, 1) from one 32-bit word, offset by half a step so
that neither 0 nor 1 comes out.
defs.intent: A uniform number in (0, 1) from one 32-bit word, offset by half a step so that neither 0 nor 1 comes out.

defs.doc: Word k (0 to 3) of a Philox block.
defs.intent: Word k (0 to 3) of a Philox block.

defs.doc:
The estimates from the five averages <e>, <e^2>, <|m|>, <m^2>, <m^4>
over some set of sweeps: the specific heat per site
beta^2 N (<e^2> - <e>^2), the susceptibility beta N (<m^2> - <|m|>^2)
and Binder's cumulant 1 - <m^4> / (3 <m^2>^2).
defs.intent: The estimates from the five averages <e>, <e^2>, <|m|>, <m^2>, <m^4> over some set of sweeps: the specific heat per site beta^2 N (<e^2> - <e>^2), the susceptibility beta N (<m^2> - <|m|>^2) and Binder's cumulant 1 - <m^4> / (3 <m^2>^2).

defs.doc:
The integrated autocorrelation time of the series x, in sweeps:
tau = 1/2 + sum_{t=1}^{W} rho(t), with the window W the first one at
which W >= WINDOW_C tau(W) (Sokal's automatic windowing), at most n / 4.
A constant series has tau = 1/2.
defs.intent: The integrated autocorrelation time of the series x, in sweeps: tau = 1/2 + sum_{t=1}^{W} rho(t), with the window W the first one at which W >= WINDOW_C tau(W) (Sokal's automatic windowing), at most n / 4. A constant series has tau = 1/2.
